extracted.intended_audience: inventors, patent applicants, patent attorneys, and Patent Office officials (practitioners working with US patent applications under the 1836 Act)
extracted.subtask_description: Requirements, procedures, and substantive standards under the U.S. Patent Act (1836) governing formation of the Patent Office, application content and formalities, examination and appeals, caveats and reissues, assignment recording, and remedies for infringement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishment and duties of the Patent Office and Commissioner
rubrics_metrics.description: There shall be established ... an office to be denominated the Patent Office; the chief officer ... called the Commissioner of Patents, to be appointed by the President ... whose duty it shall be, under the direction of the Secretary of State, to superintend, execute, and perform all such acts and things touching and respecting the granting and issuing of patents ... and shall have the charge and custody of all the books, records, papers, models, machines, and all other things belonging to said office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commissioner is responsible for administering patent grants, custody of records and models, and performing acts provided for or later directed by law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appointment, staffing, salaries, and disqualification from patent interests
rubrics_metrics.description: Commissioner may appoint a chief clerk, examining clerk, other clerks, a machinist, and messenger with specified salaries; commissioner, clerks, and every other person appointed ... shall be disqualified and interdicted from acquiring or taking, except by inheritance, during the period for which they hold appointment, any right or interest, directly or indirectly, in any patent for an invention or discovery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Staffing levels and pay are prescribed; appointees must not acquire patent interests during tenure (conflict-of-interest restriction).

rubrics_metrics.name: Oaths and bonds for officeholders
rubrics_metrics.description: Principal officer and every other person to be appointed shall, before entering upon duties, make oath or affirmation to faithfully execute the trust; commissioner and chief clerk shall give bonds with sureties to the Treasurer (commissioner $10,000; chief clerk $5,000) conditioned to render true and faithful account quarterly of all moneys received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formal oath/bond requirements for those administering patent funds and records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office seal and certified copies as competent evidence; copy fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Commissioner shall cause a seal to be made; copies of records, books, papers, or drawings under the signature of the commissioner (or chief clerk when vacant) with the seal affixed, shall be competent evidence; certified copies available on payment of ten cents for every page of one hundred words and reasonable expense for copies of drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certified copies from the Patent Office are admissible evidence; fees for written copies and drawings specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and recordation of patents; term and title requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: All patents ... shall be issued in the name of the United States, under the seal of said office, signed by the Secretary of State and countersigned by the commissioner, and shall be recorded ... Every such patent shall contain a short description or title of the invention ... correctly indicating its nature and design, and in its terms grant ... for a term not exceeding fourteen years, the full and exclusive right and liberty of making, using, and vending ... referring to the specifications for particulars, a copy of which shall be annexed ... specifying what the patentee claims as his invention or discovery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patents must have a short accurate title, refer to annexed specifications and claims, be signed/recorded, and grant exclusive rights for a statutory term (≤14 years under this act).

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive patentability eligibility (novelty and usefulness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person having discovered or invented any new and useful art, machine, manufacture, or composition of matter, or any new and useful improvement ... not known or used by others before his discovery or invention thereof, and not, at the time of his application, in public use or on sale, with his consent or allowance ... may make application ... and the commissioner ... may grant a patent therefor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invention must be new (not previously known/used/patented/described) and useful; no public use or sale with applicant's consent prior to application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written description and enablement requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Before any inventor shall receive a patent ... he shall deliver a written description of his invention and of the manner and process of making, constructing, using, and compounding the same, in such full, clear, and exact terms, avoiding unnecessary prolixity, as to enable any person skilled in the art ... to make, construct, compound, and use the same.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Descriptions must be sufficiently full, clear, and exact to enable a person skilled in the art; avoid unnecessary prolixity. This is the statutory enablement/written-description standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Machine-specific disclosure: explain principle and modes
rubrics_metrics.description: In case of any machine, he shall fully explain the principle, and the several modes in which he has contemplated the application of that principle ... by which it may be distinguished from other inventions; and shall particularly specify and point out the part, improvement, or combination which he claims as his own invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For machines, applicant must disclose the operating principle and alternative modes and must particularly point out the claimed parts or combinations (precise claiming).

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings, specimens, witness attestation, and models
rubrics_metrics.description: He shall accompany the whole with a drawing or drawings, and written references, where the nature of the case admits of drawings, or with specimens of ingredients ... sufficient in quantity for the purpose of experiment ... which descriptions and drawings, signed by the inventor and attested by two witnesses, shall be filed in the Patent Office; and he shall moreover furnish a model of his invention, in all cases which admit of a representation by model, of a convenient size to exhibit advantageously its several parts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where applicable, include drawings signed and attested by two witnesses; specimens for compositions; and a model when representation by model is possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventor's oath regarding originality and citizenship
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant shall also make oath or affirmation that he does verily believe that he is the original and first inventor or discoverer ... and that he does not know or believe that the same was ever before known or used; and also of what country he is a citizen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affirmation of originality and disclosure of citizenship required; may be made before authorized person.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissioner's examination for prior invention/publication/public use/on-sale
rubrics_metrics.description: On the filing of any such application ... the commissioner shall make, or cause to be made, an examination ... and if ... it shall not appear ... that the same had been invented or discovered by any other person in this country prior ... or that it had been patented or described in any printed publication ... or had been in public use or on sale ... if the commissioner shall deem it sufficiently useful and important, it shall be his duty to issue a patent therefor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The commissioner examines novelty, prior publication, and prior public use/on-sale and also assesses sufficiency of utility/importance before issuing a patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissioner notice and opportunity to amend or withdraw
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever ... it shall appear ... that the applicant was not the original and first inventor ... or that the description is defective and insufficient, he shall notify the applicant, giving him, briefly, such information and references as may be useful in judging of the propriety of renewing his application, or of altering his specification to embrace only that part ... which is new.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commissioner must provide brief information/references enabling applicant to decide whether to amend specification or withdraw; withdrawal entitles partial refund ($20) upon relinquishing model.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal and refund on relinquishing model
rubrics_metrics.description: If the applicant shall elect to withdraw his application, relinquishing his claim to the model, he shall be entitled to receive back twenty dollars, part of the duty required by this act, on filing a notice in writing of such election in the Patent Office; ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure and partial refund available when applicant withdraws and relinquishes model.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requiring renewed oath if persisting after objection
rubrics_metrics.description: But if the applicant ... shall persist in his claims for a patent, with or without any alteration in his specification, he shall be required to make oath or affirmation anew.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When persisting in application after notification of defects or prior art, applicant must reaffirm oath.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board of examiners on appeal from commissioner
rubrics_metrics.description: If the specification and claim shall not have been so modified as, in the opinion of the commissioner, shall entitle the applicant to a patent, he may, on appeal ... have the decision of a board of examiners, to be composed of three disinterested persons, one of whom at least to be selected ... for his knowledge and skill in the particular art ... who shall be under oath ... Said board shall be furnished with a certificate ... stating the particular grounds of his objection ... the board ... may reverse the decision of the commissioner, either in whole or in part, and their opinion being certified to the commissioner, he shall be governed thereby ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeal mechanism: three disinterested examiners (one with relevant art skill) hear appeals; fee $25 to treasury; examiners compensated (up to $10 each). Board gives notice and considers evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and proceedings for interfering applications (priority disputes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever an application shall be made for a patent which, in the opinion of the commissioner, would interfere with any other patent for which an application may be pending, or with any unexpired patent which shall have been granted, it shall be the duty of the commissioner to give notice thereof to such applicants, or patentees, as the case may be; and if either shall be dissatisfied ... he may appeal ... and the like proceedings shall be had, to determine which ... is entitled to receive a patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commissioner must notify parties of potential interference; appeal and board proceedings handle priority disputes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign patent publication within six months not necessarily fatal to US right
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in this act shall be construed to deprive an original and true inventor of the right to a patent ... by reason of his having previously taken out letters-patent therefor in a foreign country, and the same having been published, at any time within six months next preceding the filing of his specification and drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A foreign patent/publication within six months prior to US filing does not automatically bar a US patent to the original inventor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Option to date patent from filing and to file specification privately
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever the applicant shall request it, the patent shall take date from the time of the filing of the specification and drawings, not however exceeding six months prior to the actual issuing of the patent; and on like request, and the payment of the duty herein required, by any applicant, his specification and drawings shall be filed in the secret archives of the office until he shall furnish the model and the patent be issued, not exceeding the term of one year, the applicant being entitled to notice of interfering applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant may request earlier effective date (up to 6 months) and may place specification/drawings in confidential archives for up to one year on payment, preserving right to notice of interfering applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees for filing applications (citizenship/subject-based differential fees)
rubrics_metrics.description: Before any application ... shall be considered ... the applicant shall pay ... the sum of thirty dollars (if citizen or alien resident one year having sworn intention to become citizen); if a subject of the king of Great Britain, the sum of five hundred dollars; and all other persons the sum of three hundred dollars; ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differential filing payments depending on citizenship/status; payments form the Patent Fund for office expenses and salaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Succession of application rights on inventor's death
rubrics_metrics.description: Where any person hath made ... and such person shall die before any patent shall be granted therefor, the right of applying for and obtaining such patent shall devolve on the executor or administrator ... in trust for the heirs ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legal representatives can apply for the patent; application oath/affirmation varied to suit them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment recording requirement and fee
rubrics_metrics.description: Every patent shall be assignable in law ... by any instrument in writing; which assignment, and also every grant and conveyance of the exclusive right ... shall be recorded in the Patent Office within three months from the execution thereof, for which the assignee or grantee shall pay to the commissioner the sum of three dollars.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assignments and grants must be recorded within 3 months with a $3 recording fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caveat filing to preserve claim while maturing invention
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person ... who shall have invented ... and shall desire further time to mature the same, may, on paying ... twenty dollars, file in the Patent Office a caveat, setting forth the design and purpose thereof, and its principal and distinguishing characteristics, and praying protection of his right till he shall have matured his invention; ... filed in the confidential archives ... And if application shall be made by any other person within one year ... for a patent with which it may in any respect interfere, it shall be the duty of the commissioner to deposit the description, specifications, drawings, and model, in the confidential archives of the office, and to give notice by mail to the person filing the caveat, who shall, within three months ... file his description, specifications, drawings, and model; and if ... the specifications of claim interfere ... like proceedings may be had as in the case of interfering applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Caveat preserves rights while maturing; $20 fee credited toward later application; triggers notice and short window (3 months) to file full application upon interfering application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reissue for defect or inadvertent overclaiming (non-fraudulent)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever any patent ... shall be inoperative, or invalid, by reason of a defective or insufficient description or specification, or by reason of the patentee claiming ... more than he had a right to claim as new; if the error has arisen by inadvertency, accident, or mistake, and without any fraudulent or deceptive intention, it shall be lawful for the commissioner, upon the surrender to him of such patent, and the payment of the further duty of fifteen dollars, to cause a new patent to be issued to the said inventor, for the same invention, for the residue of the period then unexpired ... in accordance with the patentee's corrected description and specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reissue available to correct inadvertent defects or overclaims (non-fraudulent) on surrender and $15 fee; reissue has retroactive legal effect for subsequent causes of action as though corrected originally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annexation of later improvements to original patent
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever the original patentee shall be desirous of adding the description and specification of any new improvement of the original invention ... he may ... and on the payment of fifteen dollars ... have the same annexed to the original description and specification; and the commissioner shall certify on the margin the time of its being annexed and recorded; and the same shall hereafter have the same effect in law ... as though it had been embraced in the original description and specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure and fee ($15) to append later improvements to original patent with certificate of annexation and legal effect equivalent to original inclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedies for infringement: treble damages up to three times verdict
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever ... a verdict shall be rendered for the plaintiff in such action, it shall be in the power of the court to render judgment for any sum above the amount found by such verdict as the actual damages sustained by the plaintiff, not exceeding three times the amount thereof, according to the circumstances of the case, with costs; and such damages may be recovered by action on the case ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts may award up to treble damages (up to 3x actual damages) and costs depending on circumstances; actions may be brought in courts of competent jurisdiction in name(s) of interested parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defendant's permitted defenses and required notice of special matter
rubrics_metrics.description: The defendant ... shall be permitted to plead the general issue, and to give this act and any special matter in evidence, of which notice in writing may have been given to the plaintiff ... thirty days before trial, tending to prove that the description and specification ... does not contain the whole truth ... or contains more than is necessary ... or that the patentee was not the original and first inventor ... or that it had been described in some public work anterior ... or had been in public use or on sale ... or that he had surreptitiously or unjustly obtained the patent ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defendant must provide written notice 30 days before trial of special matters relied on; notice must identify grounds (prior use/publication, insufficiency, fraud, etc.) and names/places of prior users where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to state prior users' names and residences when relying on prior use
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever the defendant relies in his defence on the fact of a previous invention, knowledge, or use of the thing patented, he shall state, in his notice of special matter, the names and places of residence of those whom he intends to prove to have possessed a prior knowledge of the thing, and where the same had been used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific identity and residence of witnesses/prior users must be provided in advance to support prior-use defense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection for bona fide belief of originality regarding foreign prior use
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever it shall satisfactorily appear that the patentee, at the time of making his application for the patent, believed himself to be the first inventor or discoverer of the thing patented, the same shall not be held to be void on account of the invention or discovery ... having been before known or used in any foreign country, it not appearing that the same or any substantial part thereof had before been patented or described in any printed publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good-faith belief by patentee in being first inventor protects against invalidation due to foreign prior use unless prior printed publication or patent exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Court discretion where specification claims more than inventor had right to claim
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever the plaintiff shall fail to sustain his action on the ground that in his specification of claim is embraced more than that of which he was the first inventor, if it shall appear that the defendant had used or violated any part of the invention justly and truly specified and claimed as new, it shall be in the power of the court to adjudge and award as to costs, as may appear to be just and equitable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court can tailor costs/awards equitably when plaintiff over-claimed but defendant infringed actual, properly claimed parts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equitable remedy for interfering patents or adverse examiner decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever there shall be two interfering patents, or whenever a patent on application shall have been refused on an adverse decision of a board of examiners ... any person interested ... may have remedy by bill in equity; and the court ... may adjudge and declare either the patents void in the whole or in part, or inoperative or invalid in any particular part ... and may also adjudge that such applicant is entitled ... to have and receive a patent for his invention ... such adjudication ... shall authorize the commissioner to issue such patent, on his filing a copy of the adjudication ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interference and adverse examiner decisions can be litigated in equity; courts may cancel or limit patents and direct issuance of patents to prevailing applicants; judgments affect only parties and their successors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal court jurisdiction and equitable relief (injunctions) for patent cases
rubrics_metrics.description: All actions, suits, controversies, and cases arising under any law ... granting ... exclusive right ... shall be originally cognizable, as well in equity as at law, by the Circuit Courts of the United States, or any District Court having the power and jurisdiction of a Circuit Court; which courts shall have power ... to grant injunctions ... to prevent the violation of the rights of any inventor ... on such terms and conditions as said courts may deem reasonable: Provided ... that ... a writ of error or appeal ... shall lie to the Supreme Court ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent litigation proceeds in federal courts with both legal and equitable remedies; injunctions available; appeals to Supreme Court as in other federal judgments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reissue effect in law for subsequent causes of action
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent, so reissued, together with the corrected description and specification, shall have the same effect and operation in law, on the trial of all actions hereafter commenced for causes subsequently accruing, as though the same had been originally filed in such corrected form, before the issuing out of the original patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A reissued patent operates for subsequent causes of action as if the corrected description had been the original, preserving legal effect going forward.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for applying for extension of patent term
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever any patentee ... shall desire an extension of his patent beyond the term of its limitation, he may make application therefor, in writing, to the Commissioner of the Patent Office, setting forth the grounds thereof; and the commissioner shall, on the applicant's paying the sum of forty dollars to the credit of the treasury ... cause to be published in one or ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patentee may apply for term extension by written application stating grounds and paying $40; publication to be caused by commissioner (procedure continues beyond chunk).
